title: feat(R9-CI-SKIP): closure-aware heavy-lane skip in tests.yml
body:
Make the heavy Tests lanes closure-aware so they report `skipped` when a
fresh run provably cannot change the answer (the owner-commissioned CI
lever, 2026-10-12). A skipped required check satisfies the merge rule --
measured on the isolated probe, both arms (dev/programme/HANDOVER.md's
ruleset notes) -- so this pull request touches no ruleset and no repo
setting; that was verified from the probe evidence before relying on it.

One decision instrument, tests/lane_skip.py, wired through closure-scope
outputs and lane `if:` guards (job-level for `browser` and `coverage`, whose
exact check names survive a skip; step-level for the matrixed `fast`, which
reports SUCCESS while standing down); green proofs recorded only after a
lane actually ran, in a new lane-proofs job:

* **Level 1, identical base** -- a lane's green run is recorded in
  actions/cache keyed (lane, branch, diff-content-hash of the three-dot
  patch, merge-base commit). The same diff at the same merge base is the
  identical tree byte for byte, so a lane that already passed cannot
  answer differently. Holds for every lane, closures or none. Keyed on
  the commit, not its tree sha: two commits can share a tree while the
  history entities.py reads moved.
* **Level 2, moved base** (fast, coverage) -- main's delta
  (recorded base..current base) resolved through tests/closures.json
  exactly as `select` resolves a diff: empty intersection with the
  selected scripts' measured closures skips; any intersection, any gate
  file, or any file no closure has measured runs -- fail-closed onto the
  expensive answer, the same refusal `select` makes for a diff.

Scope, by measured wall cost: `fast` (median 4.0 min, p90 38.2 min on
dispatch runs; 46.7 min median on push runs) and `coverage` (p90 38.9
min) get both levels; `browser` (constant 3.8-4.0 min) gets Level 1 only
-- its driver is NOT_A_TEST and no closure has ever measured it, so only
the identical-base case is provable; `mutation` stays always-running
(0.6 min at median and max across the last 60 runs -- below the wiring's
own overhead); `slow` is nightly-only; the cheap governance lanes are
untouched. A push to main never skips: the decision steps run on
pull_request and the recheck dispatch only, and every other event leaves
the lane `if:` conditions unset, which reads as RUN -- CLAUDE.md rule 1's
forced full stays forced. The recheck dispatch gains a `no-skip` input
that forces every lane to run. Every failure of the mechanism -- cache
miss, eviction, a fork pull request's cache scope, a malformed state file
-- is a RUN, never a skip.

The latency trade, stated once: a main-side break inside a skipped
closure is no longer caught by this pull request's rerun; it is caught
one merge later, by the push-to-main FULL unscoped run on the merged
tree -- the same backstop that already underwrites GATE_SCOPE=auto. The
lever extends the closures table's trust from the pull request's own
diff to main's delta; the table is wrong in exactly the worlds where the
scoped gate is already wrong, and the same full run catches both.

## Head

`8f8982f993f847ffb10d59a05e85f19906a3bb2d` merges main `59b7660` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`a170196f0` -- the second empty-commit re-demo head over the step-level fix -- (over the closures-autofix bot's `ci: re-record closures`
`282054566` and the empty-commit demo head `d7f778529`; everything below was
measured at the first head `3b31993e9`, branched off `81acae2b7`, the #2132
merge, unless a figure names its own head).

## Mutation proof

Two mutants of `decide()` in tests/lane_skip.py, everything else at the
head, restored after each (`git status --short` clean):

1. always-skip -- `return _skip(2, "MUTANT always-skip")` inserted as the
   first statement of `decide`:
   `python3 tests/lane_skip.py self-test` -> rc 1, `7/20 pins passed`
   (13 red); among the red arms is the planted-defect guard rail -- a
   main delta of `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/const.py` with
   `tests/env_drift.py` selected MUST land on RUN.
2. always-run -- the same insertion with `_run`:
   rc 1, `12/20 pins passed` (8 red); among them the exact Level 1 case
   (identical base and diff -> skip).
3. Unmodified head: rc 0, `20/20 pins passed`.

The same self-test runs on every pull request (governance.yml's
instrument-self-tests step, the pull request's own copy), and
tests/entities.py runs it and separately pins the planted-defect decision
and the gate-file/NOT_A_TEST classification, so an edit that breaks the
decision reddens the suite instead of skipping quietly.

## Null control

The unmodified mechanism, end to end, on this pull request's own CI -- and
the demo did its job: it caught a real defect in the first wiring.

- Run 38315199590 (bot head `282054566`): every lane ran green, closure-scope
  printed `LANE: fast -- RUN ... no recorded green run for this lane and
  diff` (the negative control), and `lane-proofs` recorded all three proofs
  (cache keys logged: `lane-proof-{fast,coverage,browser}-feat/ci-closure-skip-cb0c1d5a...-d214c53a...`).
- Run 38322500356 (demo head `d7f778529`, an empty commit: identical
  three-dot diff, identical base): closure-scope decided `SKIP (level 1)` for
  all three lanes, each line naming both SHAs ("identical base d214c53a...
  and identical diff: the tree under test is byte-for-byte the tree this lane
  already passed on"). `browser` and `coverage` reported conclusion SKIPPED
  with their exact required names -- the skip satisfying the merge rule live,
  on this repository and not only the probe. But `fast`, a MATRIX job skipped
  at the job level, reported its check as `fast` -- NOT `fast (3.14)`, the
  ruleset's required context -- which would have left the merge rule waiting
  for a check that never reports. The HANDOVER's probe note says exactly this
  ("a matrix change is a required-set change") and the first wiring missed
  it; the demo head is the evidence. Fix at `52bc9441e`: `fast` stands down
  at the STEP level and reports SUCCESS (which the rule accepts without any
  ruleset edit -- none is made anywhere in this pull request); `browser` and
  `coverage` keep the job-level skip their exact names make sound.
- Re-demo, run 38332831291 at `a170196f0` (second empty commit over the fix,
  same three-dot diff): closure-scope decided `SKIP (level 1)` for all three
  lanes; `browser` and `coverage` and `coverage-ratchet` reported conclusion
  SKIPPED; `fast (3.14)` reported SUCCESS with exactly one executed step --
  "fast: closure-scope decided 'skip' for this base and diff" -- and
  `./tests/run.sh` invoked zero times in the job log. The required contexts
  are all present under their exact names and satisfied; the merge rule
  needs no ruleset change. What the lever bought on this one run: the
  instrumented suite and the coverage tree, which cost 46.7 and 48.4 minutes
  at the head before it, did not run at all.

## Figures

- `python3 tests/lane_skip.py self-test` -> `20/20 pins passed`, rc 0.
- `python3 tests/lane_skip.py state --lane fast --base abc --diff def` ->
  one line of JSON, `{"version": 1, "lane": "fast", ...}`.
- Lane wall costs, computed from `gh api
  repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/actions/runs/38293720450/jobs` and the
  sibling runs `gh run list --workflow tests.yml --limit 60` returns
  (started_at/completed_at per job, dispatch and push events split):
  fast (3.14) median 4.0 / p90 38.2 / push 46.7 min; coverage 0.6 / 38.9
  / 48.4; browser 3.8 / 4.0 / 4.0; mutation 0.6 everywhere.
- `python3 tests/structure.py` -> `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`;
  `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` -> `ALL 93 closure shrink pins
  PASSED`; `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff 81acae2b7` ->
  `MODE: FULL -- tests/closure.py changes the gate itself` (this pull
  request's own gate is full: gate files are in its diff).

## Red checks

`closures` at head `0d309106f` (job 115030109984), quoted from the job log:
"UNDER-SCOPED: tests/entities.py really reads 1 file(s) the committed closure
does not list" -- `tests/lane_skip.py`, opened by the entities block's
subprocess self-test of the new instrument. Cause: a file a gate script newly
reads needs its closure row in the same pull request, and the committed table
predated the file; not a defect in the decision logic (the self-test passed
inside `fast`). Resolution: the closures-autofix chain repaired it unaided
(`ci: re-record closures`, head `282054566`), and `closures` is green at that
head. Cheaper detector: none exists that is cheaper -- the red WAS the
existing detector working, the same-run re-record that caught the new
dependency at zero added standing cost, and the bot's repair is the designed
disposition for exactly this class (.cursor/rules/ci-autofix.md: do not
duplicate it; the Linux strace recording the bot merged is the one that
counts). The finding is that none exists: the red is the closure ratchet
working at its designed point, one run, no seat, no added standing cost.

## Forward-carry

none

## Friction

none
